hero.title: What kind of house should we live in? The quiz to take as a couple
hero.titleHighlight: What kind of house should we live in?
hero.description: Can't decide between a city apartment and a house with a garden? You each answer 12 questions about the life you picture. Then the quiz shows you the home that would suit your couple best.
hero.subtitle: 12 questions • 3 minutes each • on one phone

section1.title: How the quiz works
section1.p1: This quiz is a game to play as a couple. It helps you find the kind of place where you'd be happy, for example in the city or surrounded by fields. It asks 12 questions about your everyday life. For example, it asks what you see out of the window in the morning and what you do on a Saturday night.
section1.p2: Take the question about renovation work. You can choose between “never, we just want to unpack”, “a coat of paint, no more”, “we like a bit of DIY at the weekend” and “redoing it all ourselves, the project of a lifetime”. If you answer “never”, the quiz gives points to homes where there's nothing to do, like the architect-designed house. If your partner answers “redoing it all ourselves”, it gives points to the fixer-upper. At the end, the quiz adds up your answers and keeps the home with the most points.
section1.p3: The first person answers the 12 questions and then passes the phone. The second person answers without seeing what the first one chose. Then the quiz shows you your home as a couple, with its photo. It also shows the home each of you would have picked alone and the list of questions where you gave different answers.
section1.p4: You can also take the quiz on your own and answer for your couple. But you won't be able to compare your answers, and that's the most interesting part.

section2.title: The 10 homes in the quiz
section2.intro: The quiz can give 10 results. Some are very classic, like the house with a garden. Others are much less so, like the houseboat or the camper van. Here's who each home suits best.

section3.title: Choosing where to live together: the subjects to talk about
section3.intro: When you look for a home together, it's not only a matter of taste. There are four subjects it's better to talk about before you start viewing places.
section3.sub1Text: This is the most common disagreement. For example, one of you grew up in a village and feels stifled in the city. The other can't imagine living a twenty-minute drive from the nearest bakery. Before you look at listings, tell each other about an ordinary day in the place you picture. You'll soon see where the problem is.
section3.sub2Text: A house that needs redoing costs less to buy but it takes up a lot of weekends. If one of you loves DIY and the other hates it, the building work soon becomes something you argue about. Agree on what you can do yourselves and on the budget. Also ask yourselves how long you're willing to live in the dust.
section3.sub3Text: There are several questions to settle before you sign. Are you buying or renting? And who pays what if one of you earns more than the other? Couples who move in together for the first time often discover these questions along the way.
section3.sub4Text: Living together doesn't mean sharing everything. Some people need a room of their own, for example a study or a workshop. Some couples even choose to live in separate homes, and that doesn't stop them loving each other. Ask yourselves what kind of couple you are. A very close couple and a more independent couple don't look for the same home.

section4.title: What if you don't agree?
section4.p1: It almost always happens and it's rather a good sign, because it means each of you answered honestly. Look at the list of your different answers. If they're about the style or the size of the home, you'll find a compromise easily. If they're about city or countryside, take the time to talk about it. The same goes if one of you would rather live in separate homes.
section4.p2: Think about what comes with the house too. With a garden, you can have a dog. With an extra bedroom, you have room for a child one day. So the home you choose also depends on the life you're planning.

section5.title: What you should know about this quiz
section5.p1: This quiz is a game. It doesn't know your budget and it doesn't know property prices near you either. It only tells you what kind of place your answers lead to. It's mostly a way to start the conversation in your couple.
section5.p2: Your answers aren't saved, they stay on your phone. We only count which result you get, to see which ones come up most. Your name isn't saved either. The photos were created for this page.

seo.faq1A: The quiz can give 10 results: the house with a garden, the city apartment, the country house, the loft, the architect-designed house, the tiny house, the fixer-upper, the camper van and the houseboat. The last result is called “two apartments across the hall”. It's for couples who'd rather each have their own place.
seo.faq2Q: How is the result worked out?
seo.faq2A: Each answer gives points to the homes that match it. For example, if you answer “a restaurant or a bar ten minutes' walk away” to the question about Saturday night, the city apartment and the loft get points but the country house doesn't. When you take the quiz together, it adds up your answers and the home with the most points becomes your home as a couple.
seo.faq3Q: Can you take the quiz on your own?
seo.faq3A: Yes. Just choose “On my own, for our couple” and answer with your couple in mind. You'll get a result but you won't be able to compare your answers.
seo.faq4Q: House or apartment: how do you choose as a couple?
seo.faq4A: The simplest thing is to look at what your week is like. If you go out a lot and you don't want to look after a garden, a well-located apartment will suit you better. If you often have people over or if you're thinking of growing the family, you'll need a house instead. The quiz asks each of you exactly that kind of question.
seo.faq5Q: What if one of us would rather live alone?
seo.faq5A: That's not necessarily a bad sign. Some couples choose to live in separate homes to keep their habits. They're very happy that way. The quiz even has a result for that: “two apartments across the hall”. What matters is that each of you agrees.
seo.faq6A: No. Your answers stay on your phone. We only count which result you get, to see which ones come up most, and your name isn't saved.
